comment: Single source of truth for media detection. src/scraper.rs (MEDIA_EXTENSIONS, media_kind) and extension/media-scan.js (MEDIA_EXTENSIONS, mediaKind) each keep their own literal, and both test suites assert against this file, so the two cannot drift. See docs/adr/0011-one-playlist-parser.md.
matching: KEI-61 replaced a case-insensitive substring test over the whole URL with the final extension of the URL PATH, query and fragment excluded. The substring test matched .mp4 in '?next=.mp4' and in 'poster.mp4.jpg', and .ts in most of a modern site's TypeScript. Signed URLs still match, because an extension lives in the path: '/video.m3u8?token=...' has one.
segment_rule: A .ts path is media only when its filename stem carries a digit, the way a packager names segments (seg-001.ts, video32.ts) and hand-written TypeScript does not (main.ts). A segment beside its own playlist is collapsed into it, so this decides only the rare segment with no playlist in sight.

detection_cases.why: a signed playlist: the extension is in the path
DASH is classified, and labelled experimental
a fragment is not part of the path
a packager-named segment without a separator
TypeScript source: no digit in the stem
a directory named like an extension is not the filename's
the query is not the path
